bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging-first: shed **₹1,364cr** bank-guarantee exposure; reduced outstanding bond exposure; rebuilt cash to **₹880cr**.
- **Dividend restored in 2026** as a signal of restored financial strength.
- Demerger is structured as **no-dilution** for GEPIL holders (they receive JSW Energy shares on top of unchanged GEPIL holding).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Execution / continuity risk** of separating manufacturing: relies on a 5-yr JSW Energy services agreement + building an independent supply chain "very soon" — slippage would pressure core-services delivery.
- **NCLT-sanction / shareholder-vote risk** — the scheme is proposed, not yet sanctioned; retrospective 1-Jul-2025 effective date.
- **No fresh quarterly P&L disclosed** — turnaround metrics are multi-year; investors can't see current-quarter run-rate here.
- Structural dependence on the **thermal-power aftermarket** cycle and on the **GE Vernova / JSW ecosystem** for manufacturing support.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, disciplined-turnaround narrative; candid about Durgapur's underutilization and losses. Emphasis on "value over volume", cash conversion, and no-dilution shareholder alignment. Fully scripted management presentation — **no analyst Q&A to stress-test claims**, so credibility is best judged against the multi-year balance-sheet figures they disclosed.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The **buyer is JSW Energy** — a thermal/RE IPP that already backward-integrates equipment (per companies.csv it holds the GE Power boiler business / Toshiba-JSW TG JV); the 661-acre boiler/pressure-vessel plant plus a 5-yr reserved-capacity agreement deepens JSW's in-house thermal-equipment capability.
- **GEPIL becomes a near-pure asset-light services entity** with a clean balance sheet (cash ₹880cr, net worth ₹483cr) — the demerger is the last big step of the two-year cleanup (after Hydro/Gas slump sale + BHEL settlement).
- The **oOEM (third-party fleet) segment doubling** (₹162cr→₹320cr) is the quiet structural story — servicing non-GE thermal fleets widens the addressable base beyond the captive installed base.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance-sheet rebuild summarised by the deck as "8x+ Net Worth, 18x+ Bank balance, 1,364 crs. BG reduction in 2 years; declaration of Dividend in 2026".
- Net Worth series (Mar'23 → Mar'26): 227, 57, 233, 483 ₹ Crores; Bank Balance: -66, 49, 443, 880 ₹ Crores; Outstanding Bonds: 1,956, 2,128, 1,348, 764 ₹ Crores.
- ICRA long-term credit rating progression: BBB+(Neg) at Mar'23, BBB(Neg) at Mar'24, BBB(Neg) at Mar'25, BBB+(Stable) at Jun'26.
- Market capitalisation shown at 699, 1,784, 1,678 and 6,250 ₹ Crores for Mar'23, Mar'24, Mar'25 and Mar'26.
- Demerger consideration flows directly to shareholders rather than the company: "Existing number of shares owned in GEPIL will remain unchanged, while you gain direct equity participation in JSW Energy without diluting your current position in GEPIL."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Deep integration within India's power infrastructure sector with long-standing relationships with key entities like NTPC.
- Unique capabilities in emergency generator repair, reducing generation loss and improving grid availability.
- Strategic focus on high-margin, cash-accretive services and asset-light models, enhancing operational resilience.
- Strong operational excellence culture (Lean, GE Vernova Way) driving differentiation and cost optimization.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Evolving trade policies and tariff escalations — Introduced near-term volatility and tested adaptability of businesses and supply chains worldwide, requiring diversified sourcing strategies to maintain operational stability.
- Regulatory changes in emission norms — Revision of flue gas desulphurization installation norms for thermal power stations provides clarity but also imposes compliance requirements that could affect operations and costs.
- Dependence on coal-based power generation — While coal continues to play a role in India's energy mix, the strategic balancing towards renewable energy may reduce long-term demand for thermal power equipment and services.
- Execution risk in selective project participation — Measured approach to FGD equipment supply (EP) rather than full EPC undertakings limits exposure but also caps revenue potential from large turnkey projects.
- Supply chain disruptions — Global developments underscored the critical role of diversified sourcing strategies; reliance on a robust supply chain network across India and globally exposes the company to potential disruptions.

business.body:
- **What Durgapur is:** West Bengal facility making **power boiler components, pressure vessels, pipings, coal mills** for thermal plants; **~661 acres leasehold** (industrial factory unit + residential township).
- **Why exit:** utilization fell to mostly service/non-coal work; **significant underutilization 2023–2025** → **~₹27cr/yr average loss** booked in GEPIL. Management evaluated retention vs demerger and chose demerger to simplify the portfolio.
- **Acquirer:** **JSW Energy Ltd** (listed IPP) — expected to improve facility utilization given the broader Indian power-demand outlook.
- **Structure:** Scheme of Arrangement; going-concern, as-is-where-is; **retrospectively effective 1-Jul-2025** on NCLT sanction.
- **Entitlement:** **139 GEPIL shares → 10 JSW Energy shares** (third-party independent valuers + formal Fairness Opinion). **GEPIL shareholding unchanged / no dilution** — shareholders keep full GEPIL stake AND get direct JSW Energy shares.
- **Continuity safeguard:** **5-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy** reserves capacity at pre-agreed schedules/pricing so core-services execution isn't disrupted; independent supply chain being built in parallel ("full independence very soon").
- **Governance:** Board unanimously approved; shareholders invited to vote.

business.body:
- "Business restructuring: GEPIL commercial strategy frozen focusing on Services only" — the deck's stated organising principle since 2024.
- Growth in the core Services business is sought "through penetration in oOEM fleet" (third party fleet / other OEM), alongside the captive OEM installed base.
- "Expanded presence across multiple international markets, including Saudi, Turkey, Australia, UAE, Malaysia, Indonesia and Morocco".
- Key messages framed as four outcomes: "Higher profitability", "Lower project duration", "Credit rating upgrade", "Higher free cash flow"; the deck's summary line is "Grow Core Services to unlock sustainable profitability and cashflow".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] GEPIL is undertaking a Scheme of Arrangement to demerge the Durgapur business unit to JSW Energy Limited, to be transitioned on a "going concern, as-is-where-is" basis upon NCLT sanction, "retrospectively effective 1st July 2025"; the Board has unanimously approved the resolution and shareholders are being asked to vote.
- [Entitlement ratio] "Shareholders will receive 10 fully paid-up equity shares of JSW Energy (₹10 each) for every 139 fully paid-up equity shares of GEPIL (₹10 each)." The deck's worked illustration assumes market prices of INR 873 per GEPIL share and INR 550 per JSW Energy share, giving 139 GEPIL shares "equivalent to INR 121,347" and 10 JSW Energy shares "equivalent to INR 5,500".
- [Slump sale] "Hydro & Gas slump sale in FY 24-25.. INR 295 crs. boost to EBITDA" — the deck footnotes the EBITDA chart with "* Includes INR 295 crs. gain from Hydro & Gas slump sale".
- [BHEL settlement] "BHEL settlement ... ~INR 116 crs. P&L, INR 343 crs. Cash inflow and INR 423 crs. bank guarantee exposure release".
- [Vadodara] "Contract manufacturing and Leave & Licence agreement at Vadodara" listed among initiatives since 2024, with no further detail in the deck.
- [Rationale for exit] "GEPIL evaluated multiple options including the demerger of the Durgapur business or retention of the factory. GEPIL's key objectives included simplifying GEPIL's portfolio by exiting the asset, which is today under-utilized."
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: GE Power India Limited provides a comprehensive portfolio of power generation products and services, including boilers, environmental solutions like Flue Gas Desulphurization (FGD) and De-NOx systems, and a full suite of services for thermal power plants. The company serves major domestic power generation entities such as NTPC and Adani, focusing on core services, equipment upgrades, and selective equipment supply rather than full EPC contracts. Its operations are supported by an execution center in Noida and a robust global supply chain network.

- **Turbines:** IP inner casing supply, LP last-stage blades
- **Environmental Solutions:** Flue Gas Desulphurization (FGD) equipment supply (EP), ESP refurbishment

outlook.body:
- **Revenue / margin:** no explicit forward numeric guidance given; strategy is "value over volume" — high-margin, cash-accretive, faster-cash-conversion services.
- **Order inflow:** core-services order bookings have compounded ~25% (₹299cr→₹734cr); FY26 +34% in core services — management frames services as the growth engine, but gave **no FY27 inflow target number**.

outlook.body:
- Renewable energy capacity has crossed 250 GW and now accounts for nearly half of India's total installed capacity of around 520 GW, with a target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity, reinforcing a diversified and resilient energy mix.
- The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change's revision of flue gas desulphurization installation norms for thermal power stations has provided greater regulatory clarity while enabling continued reliable baseload supply alongside progressive emission reduction.

The execution center in Noida, along with a robust supply chain network across India and globally, underpins the Company's operational capabilities.
